baseline.note: Applies to DSH Desktop 0.1.9 with @deepseek-ai/* 0.1.0-rc.6. If the installer ships a newer baseline, the applier reports drift instead of guessing.

hunks.find:
/**
* UTF-8 output pinning prepended to every command. The subprocess collector
* decodes output bytes as UTF-8, but Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the last-resort
* executable fallback) writes the console/OEM code page by default, which
* garbles non-ASCII output; pwsh 7 defaults to UTF-8 and is unaffected. The
* statements ride on line 1 after `; ` separators so PowerShell error line
* numbers stay accurate.
*/
const ENCODING_PREAMBLE = "[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); ";
hunks.replace:
/**
* Model-facing command preamble prepended to every command, hardening the
* shell against the failure modes that hurt agents most:
* - `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` makes cmdlet errors TERMINATING, so a
*   failing command can no longer exit 0 with the error buried on stderr.
* - `$ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'` silences progress-bar noise
*   (Windows PowerShell 5.1 renders progress into redirected output, and it
*   also slows Invoke-WebRequest).
* - `$PSStyle.OutputRendering='PlainText'` strips ANSI styling (PowerShell
*   7.2+; the Get-Variable guard keeps 5.1 and 7.0/7.1 safe).
* - `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$true` upgrades native-command
*   failures to terminating errors (PowerShell 7.3+; guarded for 5.1, where
*   the variable does not exist — there only cmdlet errors fail fast).
* - UTF-8 output pinning: the subprocess collector decodes bytes as UTF-8,
*   but Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes the console/OEM code page by default,
*   which garbles non-ASCII output; pwsh 7 defaults to UTF-8 and is
*   unaffected.
* The statements ride on line 1 after `; ` separators so PowerShell error
* line numbers stay accurate.
*/
const COMMAND_PREAMBLE = "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'; if (Get-Variable PSStyle -ErrorAction Ignore) { $PSStyle.OutputRendering='PlainText' }; if (Get-Variable PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference -ErrorAction Ignore) { $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$true }; [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); ";

hunks.find: export { ENCODING_PREAMBLE, ENV_OVERRIDES, PwshLocalExecutor, PwshLocalExecutor as default, assertServiceablePwshConfig, candidatePwshPaths, resolvePwshPath };
hunks.replace: export { COMMAND_PREAMBLE, COMMAND_PREAMBLE as ENCODING_PREAMBLE, ENV_OVERRIDES, PwshLocalExecutor, PwshLocalExecutor as default, assertServiceablePwshConfig, candidatePwshPaths, resolvePwshPath };

hunks.find: Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed.
hunks.replace: Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Errors fail fast: the shell sets `$ErrorActionPreference` to `Stop`, so a failing cmdlet aborts the rest of the script (terminating error, non-zero exit) — wrap intentional error handling in try/catch. When a command's output must be parsed, print the final value with `ConvertTo-Json -Compress` (add `-Depth N` for deep structures) instead of formatted tables. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed.

hunks.find: text: "Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]` markers; investigate failures before moving on. On Windows a killed process settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker; treat a bare exit 1 after an interruption as a termination, not a command failure."
hunks.replace: text: "Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]` markers; investigate failures before moving on. pwsh commands fail fast: a failing cmdlet (or native command on PowerShell 7.3+) aborts the script and reports the error — do not write commands that depend on errors continuing silently. On Windows a killed process settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker; treat a bare exit 1 after an interruption as a termination, not a command failure."
